X_description: A left/right annulus cue whose visibility and fixed/no/random location regime were manipulated before target detection.
awareness_measure: Post-task cue-location discrimination with 80/120 trials, plus visible-cue ceiling performance.
objective_visibility_test_reason: The two-alternative task directly tested cue location against 50% chance, used participant-level binomial classification, and directed attention to the cue, making it conservative relative to the main task.
A_reason: Same-stimulus post-task localization validated chance-level cue access for the analyzed invisible groups; the validation's explicit attention to the cue would not plausibly lower awareness.
critical_dependency_reason: The candidate article and supplied supplement were checked; no classification-critical external dependency was required for this comparison.
awareness_effect_route_reason: A-validated, E-diagnostic, and F-meaningful make the structured direct comparison viable.
unaware_capacity_route_reason: A-validated and F-meaningful permit the whole unseen mapping to be tested.
null_equivalence_route_reason: The focal direct comparison did not warrant a null/equivalence claim; no null upgrade was attempted.
result_inspection_reason: Results were inspected only for the frozen E diagnostic where applicable, the unaware-capacity route, the direct same-Y awareness comparison, and required statistical/Meyen audits.
first_order_measure: Cue-location discrimination; visible and masked cue regimes were not matched in first-order evidence.
E_reason: The fixed/no/random location mapping shows qualitative selectivity: invisible cues produce fixed-location cuing without aftereffect, visible cues produce aftereffect without fixed-location cuing, while both cue in random blocks.
E_competing_account: Greater cue evidence should monotonically strengthen the same location-prioritization mapping.
E_competing_prediction: Visible cues should show the invisible cue's fixed-location benefit at least as strongly and should not reverse which temporal component appears.
E_violating_pattern: Fixed-cue benefit occurred only when invisible, whereas a negative no-cue aftereffect occurred only when visible; random-cue benefits were similar.
E_same_Y_reason: All components measure target-detection RT as a function of the same cue location across temporal regimes; they form one location-prioritization mapping.
